¡Bienvenido a la aplicación Lectura Pública de la Biblia! La lectura pública de la Biblia retoma la práctica de leer y escuchar las Escrituras en comunidad.
Leer la Biblia en comunidad fue fundamental para la vida del pueblo de Dios en el Antiguo y Nuevo Testamento. Las lecturas públicas de las Escrituras sirvieron como un acto de recuerdo y formación de identidad. Esta práctica se encuentra en toda la Biblia, desde el tiempo de Moisés con la lectura de la Ley hasta las reformas del rey Josías y la renovación que trajo al pueblo de Israel un líder como Esdras.
En la época de Jesús, leer la Ley y los Profetas en voz alta en las sinagogas era un elemento central de la vida judía. Los primeros cristianos mantuvieron esta tradición y las cartas del apóstol Pablo se leyeron en voz alta en sus reuniones. Esta práctica era tan importante para Pablo que en 1 Timoteo 4:13, instruyó a todos diciendo ""... dedícate a la lectura pública de las Escrituras, y a enseñar y animar a los hermanos"" (NVI).
La Palabra es el alimento del pueblo de Dios. Reunirse regularmente para leerla y escucharla hace que conocer y amar la Palabra de Dios sea tan simple como comer una buena comida. Hoy, puedes compartir esta práctica con tu comunidad.
¡Que tu comunidad crezca en el conocimiento y el amor de Dios y esté equipada para participar en su obra! ¡Gracias por ser parte de este movimiento!

Puedes elegir un plan de lectura de 20, 30, 45 o 60 minutos, según lo que funcione mejor para tu grupo. Ten en cuenta que la Biblia tarda 100 horas en leerse en su totalidad.
Dentro de los planes de lectura, cada sesión comienza y termina con un Salmo como oración de apertura y cierre. Cada sesión también incluye una lectura del Antiguo Testamento y una lectura del Nuevo Testamento.
Recomendamos hacer breves pausas (1 a 3 minutos máximo) al final de los pasajes del Antiguo Testamento y del Nuevo Testamento para que los participantes puedan reflexionar en oración sobre lo que han escuchado.
También, encontrarás videos de El Proyecto Biblia al comienzo de cada sesión. Discutir los pasajes de la Biblia al terminar la lectura, es completamente opcional pero te recomendamos que sea simplemente para compartir lo que más les gustó de la lectura; este no es un tiempo para predicar o enseñar, sino para escuchar juntos la Palabra de Dios. C++ (pronounced "cee plus plus") is a statically typed, free-form, multi-paradigm, compiled, general-purpose programming language. It is regarded as an intermediate-level language, as it comprises a combination of both high-level and low-level language features. It was developed by Bjarne Stroustrup starting in 1979 at Bell Labs as an enhancement to the C language. Originally named C with Classes, the language was renamed C++ in 1983. 

C++ is one of the most popular programming languages with application domains including systems software, application software, device drivers, embedded software, high-performance server and client applications, and entertainment software such as video games. Several groups provide both free and proprietary C++ compiler software, including the GNU Project, Microsoft, Intel and Embarcadero Technologies. C++ has greatly influenced many other popular programming languages, most notably C# and Java. 

C++ is also used for hardware design, where the design is initially described in C++, then analyzed, architecturally constrained, and scheduled to create a register-transfer level hardware description language via high-level synthesis. 

Bjarne Stroustrup began work on "C with Classes" in 1979. The idea of creating a new language originated from Stroustrup's experience in programming for his Ph.D. thesis. Stroustrup found that Simula had features that were very helpful for large software development, but the language was too slow for practical use, while BCPL was fast but too low-level to be suitable for large software development. When Stroustrup started working in Bell Labs, he had the problem of analyzing the UNIX kernel with respect to distributed computing. Remembering his Ph.D. experience, Stroustrup set out to enhance the C language with Simula-like features. C was chosen because it was general-purpose, fast, portable and widely used. The first commercial implementation of C++ was released on 14 October 1985. 

In 1983, the name of the language was changed from C with Classes to C++ (++ being the increment operator in C). In 1985, the first edition of The C++ Programming Language was released, providing an important reference to the language, since there was not yet an official standard. Release 2.0 of C++ came in 1989 and the updated second edition of The C++ Programming Language was released in 1991. New features included multiple inheritance, abstract classes, static member functions, const member functions, and protected members. In 1990, The Annotated C++ Reference Manual was published. This work became the basis for the future standard.

BibleProject is a nonprofit, crowdfunded organization that produces 100% free Bible videos, podcasts, blogs, classes, and educational Bible resources to help make the biblical story accessible to everyone everywhere.
From page one to the final word, we believe the Bible is a unified story that leads to Jesus. This diverse collection of ancient books overflows with wisdom for our modern world. As we let the biblical story speak for itself, we believe the message of Jesus will transform individuals and entire communities.

Many people have misunderstood the Bible as a collection of inspirational quotes or a divine instruction manual dropped from Heaven. Most of us gravitate toward sections we enjoy while avoiding parts that are confusing or even disturbing.

Our Bible resources help people experience the Bible in a way that is approachable, engaging, and transformative. We do this by showcasing the literary art of the Scriptures and tracing biblical themes from beginning to end. Rather than taking the stance of a specific tradition or denomination, we create materials to elevate the Bible for all people and draw our eyes to its unified message.
